A factional leader of the African Democratic Congress, Nafiu Gombe, has formally written to the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission regarding his resumption as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress. The letter, dated November 16, 2026, which was issued by Gombe and sighted by PUNCH Online on Tuesday, was titled, ‘Notification of resumption of duty as National Chairman pursuant to the declaration delivered by Hon. Justice Peter Lifu on 5th November, 2026,’ with reference number ADC/NHQ/CH/2026/001. Gombe requested that the commission update its portal to this effect and also recognise him for official purposes. On November 5, 2026, the Federal High Court in Abuja nullified the ADC leadership led by former Senate President David Mark and invalidated all decisions taken by the party under its leadership, including the emergence of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as its presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections. Justice Peter Lifu, in his judgment, declared the Mark-led Caretaker Committee illegal, nullifying the process through which it conducted the party’s presidential primary that produced Atiku as its flag bearer. Based on this, Gombe noted that owing to the “valid and subsisting judgment of the Honourable Court,” his resumption has commenced with immediate effect. The letter read, “I write in my capacity as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) to formally notify the Commission of my resumption of duty. “This notification follows the declaration delivered on the 5th day of November, 2026, by Hon. Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja Division, in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, Hon. Nafiu Bala Gombe V. African Democratic Congress & 4 Others, wherein the Honourable Court declared and affirmed my position as the National Chairman of the Party. “In obedience to the said valid and subsisting judgment of the Honourable Court, I have resumed duty as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress with immediate effect. “Accordingly, I respectfully request the Commission to take formal notice of this resumption; recognise me as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress for all official purposes, correspondence, and filings; and update the Commission’s portal accordingly.” Gombe equally noted that he had attached a “Certified True Copy of the judgement/declaration of the Honourable Court” for INEC’s record and necessary action. He assured the commission of his commitment to “constitutional order, due process and a harmonious working relationship” in the interest of democracy. On Sunday, November 15, The PUNCH reported that Gombe extended an olive branch to former Vice-President Abubakar, Mark and other party chieftains, calling for reconciliation and a united front ahead of the 2027 general elections. In an interview with the BBC Hausa Service, Gombe said he was ready to work with the party’s opposing faction to rebuild the party and strengthen the opposition, despite a recent Federal High Court judgment, which he described as a vindication of his faction’s position in the protracted leadership dispute.
